findings.summary: readerLookupWord duplicates the Reader selection normalization rule.
findings.consequence: Selection, legacy, embed, and fallback paths could drift to accept different word sets.
findings.evidence: Both validators independently trim, cap length, and reject the same whitespace and controls.
findings.recommendation: Extract one Reader-word normalizer for all paths.
verification: Compared both validators and their callers.

findings.summary: The word validator accepts lone UTF-16 surrogates that URLSearchParams silently replaces.
findings.consequence: Malformed text can be looked up as a different word containing U+FFFD instead of being rejected.
findings.evidence: The validator omits hasLoneSurrogate; a runtime probe encoded a lone surrogate as the replacement character.
findings.recommendation: Reject lone surrogates in the shared Reader-word normalizer and add high/low-surrogate URL tests.
verification: Inspected shared text-safety helpers and confirmed URLSearchParams replacement in a runtime probe.

findings.summary: Protocol event and dictionary domains are repeated in TypeScript unions and runtime validators.
findings.consequence: A future typed value could be omitted from runtime membership validation.
findings.evidence: Handwritten unions, event Set, and dictionary parser independently enumerate the same domains.
findings.recommendation: Derive union types and membership sets from shared readonly value tuples.
verification: Inspected unions, sets, parser values, and exhaustiveness behavior.
Generated and read every unit in the exact current packet.
Inspected outgoing and incoming consumers, lifecycle correlation, selection paths, complete protocol tests, shared text-safety helpers, and established surrogate guards.
